scope: One local synthetic Ollama run per topology. This review does not rank the topologies because their objectives and duties differ.
scoreReason: A single development example per topology is insufficient for a defensible capability score or reliability rate.

sourceArtifacts.reason: Preserved as incident evidence. A runtime audit-persistence defect omitted one attempted tool call; attempt 2 followed the regression-tested repair.

results.review: Suri used the calculator and correctly returned 2,600 THB for 18 times 125 plus 350. The answer clearly remained draft-only.

Suri correctly produced 2,040 THB and the document-backed four-working-day lead time. Quinn repeated the two valid tools but the model returned an empty final response, so QA failed and the workflow did not claim completion.

Suri completed three valid tool calls, then supplied a calculation expression as an order number to get_order_status. The tool rejected the unverified identifier, Suri failed without an answer, and the remaining four roles were blocked from using unconfirmed evidence.

conclusions: The local runtime enforces scope, tool permissions, evidence storage, terminal states and dependency blocking in these examples.
The small local model completed the basic individual example but was not reliable enough for the pair QA or five-role workflow.
A structural pass does not mean the business objective passed; semantic outcome and runtime safety are recorded separately.
No production LINE deployment, customer-data access, external connector action or automatic model failover was tested here.
The next effectiveness test needs repeated held-out objectives with the same duties, tools, budget and grading criteria before comparing models or team sizes.
